column5: MEASURED on all three axes off live node data, and the two deltas the previous generation left open are both settled. GEOMETRY 343x190, radius 12, padding 12 all round, vertical SPACE_BETWEEN so the declared 16 itemSpacing is inert; header row 319x54 = a 54x54 tile then a 16 gap to the question then a 98x54 gauge box at x=221; CTA row 319x44 holding two 155.5x44 buttons at gap 8, radius 12, padding 14/24; data row 319x16 at y=162, volume 82 wide at x=0 and a 42-wide cluster at x=277 whose 14x14 tag and 16x16 glyph sit 12 apart. All of that already shipped and re-checks clean. COLOUR: the No fill was the one real miss and is FIXED. That button is TWO different reds - the box is App/Red-O #FB3324 at 14% and only the letters are App/Red 300 #FF574A - where we filled with the letters red at the right alpha, compositing to (51,44,41) over the #122524 shell against the frame (51,39,36). The Yes half is what gives it away: it fills AND letters with the single #17F9B4 at 12%, so two hexes on the No half is deliberate. Shell #122524, tile stroke #123F3C, question #FFFFFF, volume #95A09F, and Chance carries 0.44 on the NODE while its fill reads #FFFFFF at 1. TYPE question and both button labels Manrope Regular 14/16 at -4%, volume Mulish Regular 12/14 at -4%, gauge readout Manrope 14/16 over Chance at Manrope 12/16 - all already on the ramp and pinned. THE ONE REMAINING DIVERGENCE IS AUTHORISED, not open: the frame draws a 14x14 icon-only pill filled Coral #FF7E50 at 34% around a 10px glyph, and we draw a text pill carrying the market CATEGORY and countdown, which is a standing ruling. That pill is drawn to its own master exactly - 1px border, radius full, 8/2 padding, Mulish 11/14 at -4% - so it measures 20 tall against the frame icon pill 14, which the card absorbs in free space at this cut.

THE DESKTOP CARD THE COMPONENT ACTUALLY IMPLEMENTS, and it was carrying an uncatalogued geometry defect. 390x224, radius 24, padding 16, SPACE_BETWEEN, three rows at 71 / 50 / 18: header y=16 h=71 (54x54 tile, 16 gap, question, 98x71 gauge at x=260), CTA y=113.5 h=50 (two 175x50 at gap 8), data y=190 h=18 (volume 96 wide at x=0, a 42-wide cluster at x=316). The two 26.5 spacings are FREE SPACE handed out by SPACE_BETWEEN, not a declared itemSpacing, so the bottom inset lands on the drawn 16 only while the three rows plus the CSS gap minimum fit the 192 content box. FIXED: the favourite heart carried 6px of padding around its 16px glyph for a 28px tap target, which made the data row measure 28 instead of the tag pill 20. That put the column at 71 + 50 + 28 + two 24 gaps = 197 against 192, SPACE_BETWEEN had no free space left to give, and the last row finished 11 from the card edge instead of 16. Cancelling the padding in the cross axis keeps the 28 target painted while the row measures 16, so the row height falls back to the tag pill 20 and the column closes at 25.5 free either side. The 1px against the frame 26.5 is the text tag we draw where the frame draws a 14px icon pill, and it is spent on the gaps rather than on the inset. COLOUR and TYPE re-confirmed at this cut: volume Mulish Regular 14/18 at -4% #95A09F, question and labels 16/22, gauge readout Mulish 16/16, shell #122524.

MEASURED and NOT CHANGED - TWO 1440 BOARDS CONTRADICT EACH OTHER ON ROW ORDER. This card is 390x224 with the same radius 24, padding 16 and the same three rows at 71 / 50 / 18 as its twin, and every interior number matches: 54x54 tile, 16 gap, 98x71 gauge, two 175x50 buttons at gap 8, a 42-wide cluster whose 14x14 coral pill and 16x16 glyph sit 12 apart, volume Mulish Regular 14/18 at -4% #95A09F. What differs is the ORDER, twice over. Here the data row is FIRST at y=16 with the header at y=60.5 and the buttons at y=158; on the twin the data row is LAST at y=190. And inside that row the cluster is on the LEFT at x=0 with the volume right-aligned at x=262, where the twin puts the volume at x=0 and the cluster at x=316. The cluster itself also reverses: glyph then pill here, pill then glyph on the twin. So it is a full 180 degree flip of the card, not a detail. Both renders were pulled and compared side by side and both are real authored boards at the same width, which makes this the CALL SITE axis rather than the viewport - it needs a decision, not a hinge. We implement the twin, which is also the node the component docblock and its oracle cite. Held at partial pending that ruling; nothing was guessed.

RE-ROUTED off UnifiedMarketCard, which is not the component that draws this. It is a two-team fixture card with THREE priced sides - 343x188, radius 12, padding 12, a 319x72 header of two 319x32 rows at gap 8, then a 319x50 CTA row of three 101x44 buttons at gap 8, radius 12, padding 14/24, then a 319x18 data row. UnifiedMarketCard is structurally binary: its market model carries a single priceUpBps for the up side and no outcome array at all, so a third side has nowhere to live and this frame could never be its job. The repo DOES draw this archetype - the sports board renders a two-team card with three priced chips per fixture - so the previous generation calling the archetype absent was measured against the wrong file. Left partial rather than promoted because that board is a different cut of the same archetype (214 tall, 30-tall chips at radius 8 against 44-tall buttons at radius 12) and reconciling the two cuts belongs to the lane that owns it.

RE-ROUTED for the same reason as its unselected twin - a three-sided fixture card is not the binary card. Same 343x190 shell, radius 12, padding 12, same 319x72 header of two 32-tall rows at gap 8 and same three 101x44 buttons. What it adds is a SELECTED state carried by four changes at once: a 2px #56C7F3 stroke, the shell fill dropping from #122524 to #052D2D, a drop shadow at 0,1 blur 4 in black at 25%, and the three button fills falling to #001615 at 80% where the unselected card holds them opaque. No card on any Predict surface carries a selection today, so all four signals are unbuilt - but they are unbuilt in the sports board, not in the binary card.

RE-ROUTED, and the previous generation defect claim against UnifiedMarketCard was false. This is the MULTI-DEADLINE card: 343x190, radius 12, padding 12, vertical gap 12 live at primary MIN, a 319x54 header at gap 16 where the question runs the full 249 to the edge because this card draws NO gauge, then a 319x72 body at y=78 of two 319x32 rows at gap 8, each row a 131-wide date, a 36-wide right-aligned percentage and a 136x32 button pair at gap 8, then a 319x16 data row at y=162. That is exactly the archetype GroupedMarketCard already builds - one heading over one row per sibling market, each row a deadline, a percentage and a Yes/No pair - reading its grouping rule from the event-group helper. So the claim that a market with two dated outcomes loses both dates and both percentages was measured against a component that never receives one. Left partial rather than promoted because the DOM of the component that does draw it has not been measured against these numbers, and it is not this lane file.

RE-ROUTED off UnifiedMarketCard, where an older generation filed it. Confirmed against live node data: this is a 738x433 wrapper whose interior is a 706x363 stack splitting into a 706x152 top row and a 706x187 bottom, and the bottom half is a PRICE CHART - a 638x153 plot with a 64x153 price column reading absolute levels, a 46x172 buys ladder and a time axis - over a 706x24 card foot carrying the volume line and a 58x24 wordmark. The top row pairs a 337x138 block (a 72x72 avatar at radius 12, a tag, a title and a timestamp, over two 164.5x50 buttons at gap 8) against a 337x152 comment feed behind two 40-tall gradient fades. None of that is a grid card: it is the market detail hero, it has no gauge and no Yes/No grid row, and the component that owns it has already been measured in full elsewhere. Recorded here only so the routing stops pointing at this lane.

RE-ROUTED off UnifiedMarketCard for the same reason as its future twin - a 738x433 detail hero carrying a chart, a comment feed and a card foot is not the 390x224 grid card. Already measured against the component that owns it, where the two masters are recorded as two LAYOUTS of one shell rather than one design. No grid-card work is implied by this frame.

RE-ROUTED off UnifiedMarketCard - the third 738x433 master in the same set, a detail hero variant that adds a fixture date to the title block. Same shell family as the future and live masters and the same owner. Listed so the grid-card lane stops inheriting it.
